# RH solution-object ledger (universal-law field)

What any proof of RH, and the missing object it needs, MUST be/have/do and CANNOT be/have/do, distilled from audited theorems, no-gos and RH-equivalent receivers. Facts only: no history, work log, route status or task list.

Conventions: each bullet is one constraint (MUST/CANNOT) or one proved fact (F…) with its consequence; E = evidence. Tags: [L] Lean-certified, [P] paper proof only, [Ls] Lean scratch only, [N] numerical only. ¬ZL = gives no zero-location/RH conclusion. Receiver = proved implication/equivalence ending in RH whose premise is unproved; producer = a proof of such a premise. Original IDs are kept for lookup; `r` marks a later entry that reused an earlier number. Paths: R:X = formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/X.lean; H:X = formal/GaloisForLFunctions/HTGeometry/X.lean; ML:X = formal/.lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib/X.lean; Pn:x = docs/drafts/pipeline/{0-backlog,1-in-progress,2-fully-proven,3-formalized,4-publication-ready,5-failed}[n]/x.md; ULF:x = P1:universal-law-field/x.

## Hard facts

- F01 Receiver abundance: many exact RH equivalences in corpus (positivity, flatness, finite action, recurrence descent, formation properness, source-dagger descent, boundary absence) = readouts, not independent evidence or producers.
- HARD LOCK P: positivity alone does not supply the missing arithmetic inequality. All-test Weil positivity RH⇔; generic finite Gram/CP/KMS constructions nonselective; stated positive Green–Stokes split exceeds its Euler budget (no-gos keep exact premises). Independently proved quantitative bound for the literal arithmetic source remains a possible producer; being positive, quadratic or contractive is not a disqualification. Gamma–Hankel PSD gives a lower covariance floor, not the missing upper ceiling (`MobiusLaplaceGammaHankelWall`: `finiteMobiusGammaHankelOffDiagonalCovariance_lower_floor`).
- F02 Finite local exactness nonselective: arbitrary finite packets, jets, multiplicities, indices, Grams, KMS systems, homology, determinants, recoveries coexist with off-line charge.
- CANNOT infer real zeros for the Fourier transform of a positive, even, double-exponentially decaying source `(H''-H/4)/2` from positive definiteness of mass log curvature `(log H)''`; these coexist with off-real zeros; sign transfer needs more structure. P5:clg-ttf-theta-power-curvature-transfer ([P] counterexample; [L] positive family).
- F03 MUST distinguish identities between functions from relations at one point: differential independence excludes nonzero polynomial identities in functions + derivatives over the coefficient field, not a common zero; finite family analytic at `a`, differentially independent over a field ⊇ `C(s)`: multiplying every function by `s-a` preserves independence, makes every value at `a` zero ⇒ independence cannot retire a relation forced only at a zeta zero. [L] `HTGeometry.differentialIndependent_mulBase_iff`; zeta-dilation application `AdjacentDilation.adjacentDilationGauge_differentialIndependent_over_zeta`. Relation at a zero needs own arithmetic proof.
- F04 Source/receiver firewall: a construction can land exactly on Xi data while its final continuity, sign, descent, properness or bound is still literally RH.
- CANNOT count a positivity identity with explicit `|Xi|²` factor as a source proof of strict positivity: centered coordinate `E(w)=(1/2+w)X(w)`: `E+E#=X`, `|E(w)|²-|E#(w)|²=2 Re(w)|X(w)|²`; defect vanishes exactly at the off-line zeros to be excluded ⇒ strictness MUST come from source-derived nonvanishing independent of this factor. P2:theta-half-line-port-alternating-orientation#additive-ports-need-a-nondegeneracy-gate.
- F05 Large fused subcorpus has one signed current `a(s) = 2 Re(s) - 1`; FE reflection sends `a` to `-a`. Gamma-six residue, Möbius prime-normal growth, Green codiagonal, Wold/Fisher response, affine Xi residue, several Hellinger/Kakutani readers recover `a`, `a²`, or its support.
- F06 FE transports, does not select: common recovery lifts FE without information or formation-capital loss; FE-symmetric entire positive countermodels can have off-line zeros.
- F07 Faithful recovery conserves obstruction: split/injective recovery preserves information, Hellinger affinity, formation capital, completion boundary; strict improvement requires erasure.
- F07a CANNOT count copied labels as independently formed data: diagonal copying preserves every coordinate marginal but = independent `d`-fold product (`d>=2`) only for a Dirac packet, even for normalized signed real weights. Two finite probability packets: one common stochastic map produces both independent products ⇔ packets identical or disjoint supports. [L] `finiteDiagonalPower_marginal`, `finiteDiagonalPower_eq_independentPower_iff_dirac`, `finiteFormationClone_exists_iff`. Matching marginals / faithful split recovery do not give that replicator; cloning argument MUST construct it.
- F08 Formation and completion do not commute: off-line current appears as completion boundary, Roos `lim¹`, physical transport; boundary absence RH⇔; finite formation never sees the class.
- F09 Bounded presentation changes are genuine gauges: mutually bounded dictionaries preserve saturation and completion boundary; ordinary naturality across bounded gauges cannot annihilate off-line class.
- F10 Quotients erase typed data differently: positive squares erase sign/phase; reduced quotients nilpotent tangents; scalar fusion homology; compact observation lifted history.

### Jensen polynomials, integrated prime error, central moments
- CANNOT certify a quartic Jensen polynomial from independent bounds on the three dispersions `D_l=m(n+l)m(n+l+2)/m(n+l+1)²−1`: along the equal-dispersion (log-normal) diagonal the tolerance is `≍1/b` (`b=n+½`; the log-normal reference is a rescaled Hermite quartic, hyperbolic for `D·b<1`), transverse to it (`D_{n+1}` alone, i.e. the second difference `D₀−2D₁+D₂`) only `≍1/b²` (perturbation terms `≍b⁴|ε|` against reference `≍b²`) ⇒ box sandwiches on moment ratios are useless at degree four. A dispersion certificate MUST give two-sided control of the size-biased theta dispersions to relative precision `O(1/n)` localised at the tilted mode (`Var(log s)·b≤1/2`, `|κ₃|≲b^{−3/2}`, `|κ₄|≲b^{−2}` for `x^{2κ}Φ(x)dx`, `κ≥n`); curvature-infimum bounds cannot (the infimum is 0 in the log variable); with these and `b≥2000` the quartic is hyperbolic [L]. (CANNOT-321, MUST-224)
- CANNOT individuate zeros in the Jensen–Pólya regime `d=o(n)`: [literature] for `n³log²(n+2)≥Kd⁵` all `J^{d,n}` of `Ξ` are hyperbolic unconditionally (Holland, arXiv:2608.08682; five Taylor ratios matched by a real-rooted finite-free product of two Jacobi factors; semicircle zero law); input: sectorial saddle asymptotic of `log M_z` (`M_z=∫Φ(u)u^{2z}du`; derivatives `2/(x𝓛_x)`, `−2/(x²𝓛_x)`, `4/(x³𝓛_x)`, `x=L(πe^L+¾)`) ⇒ `D₀b→0` like `2/log n`, `D₀−D₁≍2/(n²log n)`, `D₀−2D₁+D₂≍2/(n³log n)`; finite-order matching stops below `d≍n log n` (residual `≍(d+2√(nd))^{2K+1}/(n^{2K}(2K+1)!log n)`). RH information sits only at `d≳n`: all `J^{d,n}` for one `n` hyperbolic ⇔ `F₀^{(n)}` Laguerre–Pólya (`Ξ(t)=F₀(−t²)`), which for some `n` ⇔ finitely many non-real zeros (Pólya–Wiman, Fourier–Pólya for order `<2`) ⇒ the first non-hyperbolic degree satisfies `d*(n)≥cn^{3/5}log^{2/5}(n+2)`; a producer MUST control Taylor coefficients below the saddle threshold jointly with the asymptotic ones; the perturbative wedge is RH-blind. (CANNOT-322, MUST-225)
- MUST (and need only) prove a uniform square-root bound for the signed integrated prime error: [L] `D(X)=X−1−Σ_{n≤X}Λ(n)log(X/n)`, any finite `|D(X)|≤B√X` (`X≥1`) ⇔ RH; no small `B` required; a logarithmic loss fails the criterion; unsigned prime terms and formal source identities do not supply the signed bound. (CANNOT-323, MUST-226)
- MUST know negative central moment witnesses have degree ≥ 2: [L] `−Ξ'(t)/(tΞ(t))=ΣM_kt^(2k)` satisfies `a²M₀+2abM₁+b²M₂≥0` unconditionally (exact theta-source integration; R:ThetaGibbsSteinSourceMinor). (CANNOT-324)
- MUST control the exponent, not constants, in the fixed exponential-pole criterion: its zero margin is a constant-level artefact of test transforms with real zeros; aperture-window averages `∫_a^{a+1}E_±` remain RH⇔ (an off-line zero contributes `e^{2aβ₀}`× an oscillating sign-changing factor) and under RH are `≥0.94·c₀(e−1)e^a` (cross term `≤(e+1)Σ|ρ|^{−3}√X≈0.004√X` vs mean `≈0.079√X`); every equivalent form is von Koch's statement that `Σ_{n≤e^h}Λ(n)/√n−2e^{h/2}` grows at most polynomially in `h` (functionals against `K_a'`, `K_a(h)=4sinh(a−h/2)+2(2a−h)cosh(h/2)`). [N] with 1500 zeros the worst relative margin over `a≤A` is `0.42` (`A=10³`), `0.33/0.31` (`A=10⁶`), ≈`0.5−0.013 log A`, `>0.48` at `a=log p/2`, `p≤10⁸` ⇒ a proof losing a fixed factor below 3 is not excluded by constants; the exponent `Θ=½` excludes every known argument (sieve, mean value, positivity). ### The Weil lag function (exact form of RH as one bounded function)
Notes: P1:integer-lag-law-notes, P1:lag-ratio-law.
`Φ(L)=Σ'_ρ e^{L(ρ−½)}/(ρ(1−ρ))` (absolutely convergent for all real `L`, even, continuous); `Φ(0)=a_1=2+γ−log 4π=Σ'_ρ1/(ρ(1−ρ))` ≈ 0.046 (= first Li coefficient `λ₁`) [L]. Prime side [L]: for `X=e^L>1`, `Σ'_ρX^ρ/(ρ(1−ρ))=(X−ψ(X))+X(Σ_{n≤X}Λ(n)/n−log X+γ)−log 2π+S(X)`, `S(X)=Σ_{k≥1}X^{−2k}/(2k(2k+1))`; equivalently `Φ=Φ_arch+Σ_{n≤X}2Λ(n)n^{−1/2}sinh((L−log n)/2)` (archimedean germ + one convex kink of slope `Λ(n)/√n` per prime power); integer lags `a_n=Φ(log n)`; `√xΦ(log x)=1+γ−log 2π+∫_1^x m(t)dt+S(x)` with Mertens error `m(t)=Σ_{n≤t}Λ(n)/n−log t+γ`.
- MUST prove boundedness of `Φ`; every form is Lean-equivalent to RH, with the sharp constant built in: RH ⇔ `Φ` bounded ⇔ bounded above ⇔ bounded below ⇔ `|Φ|≤Φ(0)` ⇔ `Φ` positive-definite ⇔ `Φ` Bohr almost periodic ⇔ `∀n: a_n≤a_1` ⇔ `(a_n)` bounded above ⇔ bounded below ⇔ every arithmetic Gram matrix `(Φ(log(n/m)))_{n,m≤N}` PSD (2×2 minors on `{1,n}` are `2(a_1−a_n)`) ⇔ `Φ` bounded above on the `{p,q}`-rationals `p^kq^l` (any two primes; dense lags) ⇔ `a_p≤a_1` at all primes ⇔ bounded above on prime powers ⇔ on `k`-th powers (any `k≥1`) ⇔ Cramér's mean-square criterion `∫_1^X(ψ(t)−t)²t^{−2}dt=O(log X)` (under RH `Φ` = mean autocorrelation of `Ψ(x)=e^{−x/2}(e^x−ψ(e^x))`). Dichotomy [L]: either every `a_n∈[−a_1,a_1]` (RH) or `(a_n)` is unbounded above and below — no intermediate regime; boundedness by any `M` gives the sharp `M=Φ(0)` ("losing a constant costs nothing, losing the exponent is impossible"). Mechanism of converses: Landau (a one-sided bound makes `M∓Φ` a nonnegative density whose Laplace transform `(M+1)/s∓G(s)`, `G(s)=Σ(ρ(1−ρ))⁻¹/(s−(ρ−½))`, is analytic at every real point, so its abscissa is 0) + a zero of maximal real part on its horizontal line giving a pole with pole-free right ray. (MUST-232, MUST-235, MUST-236, MUST-237, MUST-238, MUST-240, MUST-243, MUST-244, MUST-251, MUST-252, MUST-254)
- MUST have zero margin: [L] under RH `a_1` is the exact supremum of `{a_n:n≥N}` for every `N`, approached along the powers of every base (Dirichlet approximation of finitely many `γlog b/2π`); unconditionally `limsup a_n≥a_1` (equality iff RH) ⇒ no proof can lose any constant along any `b^m`, and a proof must control the joint phases `γlog b` exactly. The floor is arithmetic: under RH `inf a_n=−a_1` ⇔ the ordinates have no odd relation (every integer relation `Σc_γγ=0` has even coefficient sum; weaker than LI); only `inf a_n<0` is forced. [L] Unconditional `Ω±(√n)`: the genus-kernel error `E(n)=√n a_n` exceeds `(a_1−ε)√n` and is `≤−η√n` infinitely often ⇒ the sign of `E(n)` is no producer; only the size of positive excursions is RH-sensitive. (MUST-239, MUST-240, MUST-241)
- MUST produce marginal, gapless positivity exactly at the true prime data: under RH on every window `[0,L]` the Toeplitz operator of `Φ` is `Σ_ρ|ρ|^{−2}|e^{iγx}><e^{iγx}|` (trace `LΦ(0)`, spectrum accumulating at 0, density `~log ξ/(2πξ²)`); moving or rescaling one kink by `ε≠0` adds a signed density `~εΛ(n)n^{−1/2}sin(ξ log n)/ξ` exceeding `log ξ/ξ²` at high frequency ⇒ not positive-definite for any `ε≠0` [theorem under RH; N]. [N] Keeping only prime powers `≤P`, positive-definiteness fails at `L=log n₁+δ`, `δ∈[0.013,0.05]` (`n₁` the next prime power; 42 truncations `P≤2048`); `|Φ_P|≤Φ(0)` fails at `log n₁+δ'`, `δ'≤2arcsinh(Φ(0)√n₁/Λ(n₁))`. ⇒ CANNOT be a producer with a uniform gap (coercivity, strict Hankel/Toeplitz PSD with margin, strictly positive symbol); CANNOT treat any finite set of primes as negligible or replace prime powers by any approximation, however accurate: positivity holds only for exact positions `log n` and weights `Λ(n)/√n`. ### Pairwise zero dynamics (Calogero heat flow)

The angular energy of a zero weights by the squared difference of displacements; the critical-line potential weights by the squared displacement. Along a path of velocity `ż = −2L` the convective derivative cancels the transport term exactly: `d/dτ V(z(τ),τ) = V_zz − 2V²`. The characteristics are not auxiliary — `−2L(z) = −2Σ_k(z − x_k)⁻¹` is the Calogero velocity field, so the zeros travel along them and the field equation carries no transport in Lagrangian coordinates. **Cannot** therefore attribute the residual loss in a collision lemma to transport. **Must:** what remains is the diffusion, and its sign is adverse where it matters: between consecutive real zeros the field tends to `+∞` at both ends, so it has an interior minimum with `V_zz ≥ 0`. The comparison is not marginal — at the midpoint of a gap `δ` the pair's own part gives `V = 8/δ²`, `V_zz = 192/δ⁴`, `2V² = 128/δ⁴`, so diffusion exceeds damping by exactly `3/2` and the raw field grows along the characteristic. **Must** consequently run any collision lemma on the regular part alone: the pair's singular part is already exact in `u' = 4Δu − 8`, but the damping bound does not apply to the raw field near a close pair.
- MUST-446 — the pair field is a pointwise value of the regular field inside the gap. Consecutiveness places every surrounding zero outside the closed gap, so `L` is differentiable there with derivative minus the regular field, and the mean value theorem gives `Δ = V(ξ)` for some `ξ` strictly inside the gap, `V(z) = Σ_y (z − y)⁻²`. **Must:** the pair quantity is an honest pointwise value of a field smooth across the gap and carrying none of the pair's singularity, so any bound on the regular field over the gap interval bounds `Δ`. **Cannot:** object that the adverse diffusion of the raw field near a close pair obstructs this — that adversity belongs to the pair's own singular part, which this identity removes.

Each term of the regular field is monotone across the gap in the direction of its own zero, so the left-hand terms are largest at the left endpoint and the right-hand terms at the right endpoint. With the pair field a pointwise value of the regular field inside the gap, this gives `Δ ≤ Σ_{y < x₁} (x₁ − y)⁻² + Σ_{y > x₂} (x₂ − y)⁻²` without locating the interior point. **Must:** neither sum carries a near-singular term, the closest contribution on each side lying at the distance of the neighbouring gap, so the pair field of a close pair is controlled by ordinary one-sided spacing data at the two zeros and the pair's own singularity is absent by construction.

- **MUST-1372 [L] (compressing multipliers remove the attainment gap of thin lag receivers).** For a multiplier `h` on the zero copies put `R_h(n) = Σ_ρ e^{n h(ρ)}/(ρ(1−ρ))`. Call `h` compressing if, for every `ε > 0`, only finitely many zero copies have `Re h > ε`.

  - (iv) `H(z) = z/log(2 − z²)` is compressing unconditionally. For `|x| ≤ ½`, `Re H(x+iy)` has the sign of `x` (via `|arg(2−z²)| ≤ 2|xy|/u` and `log u − 2y²/u ≥ log(7/2) − 1 > 0`, `u = 2 − x² + y²`). Once `log(7/4+y²) ≥ 1`, `Re H ≤ 3x/log(7/4 + y²)` (`re_logCompressedMultiplier_le`, `isCompressingMultiplier_logCompressedZeroMultiplier`). **Hence RH ⟺ `Re Σ_ρ e^{nH(ρ−½)}/(ρ(1−ρ))` is bounded above along `n ∈ ℕ` (`riemannHypothesis_iff_bddAbove_logCompressedLag`), with no ZAL or attainment premise.**

  - **CANNOT (paper, loop row 1122):** compression cannot be free. A receiver detects a zero of depth `δ` at height `γ` once `n ≳ 2log γ/(δ w(γ))`, where `w(γ) = ∂_x Re H(iγ)`. Its test function puts frequency `γ'` at position `u ≈ n w(γ')`, so it needs primes up to `γ^{(2/δ)·w_max/w(γ)}`. The lag (`w ≡ ℓ`) needs `γ^{2/δ}`. An AAL-free thin receiver must have `w(γ) → 0`, so it pays an unbounded factor `w_max/w(γ)` in the resolution exponent. That factor can grow arbitrarily slowly; for `H = z/log(2−z²)` it is `≍ log γ`.

- **MUST-1379 [L] (lag sums along all long spacings: local finiteness is the exact dividing line).**

The centres `a` with weights `2πr³` reproduce `∫e^{sx}dx · ∫e^{isy}g(y)dy` exactly on every exponential (`HTGeometry.BandLimitedPositiveConfiguration.exists_disc_configuration_of_density`; a layer cake without level sets).

The same holds if every progression `mℓ`, `m ≥ 1`, `ℓ ∈ (c, d)` samples zero (`eq_zero_of_lag_vanishing_interval_spacings`).

  - **Reading.**
    - Zero-side receivers that read the lag sum along an interval of spacings, or along every long spacing, MUST be rigid exactly for locally finite configurations. The corpus interval-of-spacings receiver (`riemannHypothesis_of_Ioo_subset_lagProgressionLevel`) MUST therefore use local finiteness, i.e. meromorphy of the Cauchy series of the zeros. It CANNOT be proved from positivity of the weights, summability and position in the strip alone.

The rigidity half shows that intervals of spacings CANNOT be reached this way.

- **MUST-1380 [L] (single-base blindness with exactly positive weights of Weil size and zero counting `O(T^ε)`).**
  - **Statement.** For every spacing `ℓ > 2 log 10` there is a countable configuration `ρ_i` with positive weights `c_i` such that:

    (`RHTower.exists_positive_lag_configuration_density_blind`.)

    - This upgrades CANNOT-515 (sector-positive weights) to exactly positive weights. It also makes rigorous the positive-weight claim of JAS row 194: Wesler's `Σ r = ∞` is an artifact of disc packings.

  - **MUST-1379 addendum [L] (dense sampling).** For a locally finite summable configuration with `|Re ρ − ½| ≤ B`, a lag sum vanishing on ANY set `D` whose closure contains a half-line has all weights zero (`RHTower.eq_zero_of_lag_vanishing_dense`, via `continuous_lagSum`). Example: the rational points `s ≥ s₀`. Reading: for a countable family of spacings `S`, the multiples `{mℓ : ℓ ∈ S}` accumulate only at multiples of accumulation points of `S` (each `mS` has its accumulation points in `m·S'`). So countable families are never dense-rigid. Zero-side rigidity MUST come from spacing sets thick enough that their multiples are dense in a half-line; the Baire receiver (MUST-1363) and intervals are of this type.

- **MUST-1381 [L] (robust zero planting across two levels of characters; resolves the core risk of the rational-lock card C2112).** Let `χ₁ ≠ χ₂` be characters mod `N` with `C(χ₁), C(χ₂) ≠ 0`. There is `η > 0`, depending only on `(N, C, χ₁, χ₂)`, such that the following holds for EVERY multiple `N'` of `N` and every `P₀`. Take coefficients `D` on the characters mod `N'` that do not factor through `N`, with `Σ|D| ≤ |C(χ₁)|/96`, and any far family `(e_j, g_j)` with `|g_j| ≤ 1` and `Σ|e_j| ≤ η`. Then some `σ > 1`, finite set `S` of primes `> P₀` and values `|z_p| ≤ p^{−σ}` give
  `Σ_ξ C(ξ)Π_S(1−ξ(p)z_p)^{−1} + Σ_ψ D(ψ)Π_S(1−ψ(p)z_p)^{−1} + Σ_j e_jΠ_S(1−g_j(p)z_p)^{−1} = 0`

    - A character mod `N'` that does not factor through `N` sums to `0` on every fibre of `(ℤ/N')ˣ → (ℤ/N)ˣ` (`sum_unitsFibre_eq_zero`). So pulling back the level-`N` model vector evenly over the fibres gives exact pairing `0` with every such character, preserves the pairing with induced characters, and keeps the `ℓ¹` norm (`charPair_pullback_of_not_factorsThrough`, `charPair_changeLevel_pullback`, `sum_norm_pullback_le`).
    - Realization by primes in the unit classes mod `N'` (`exists_realization`) then makes the band characters contribute at most `2Σ|D|`. The far terms contribute at most `2e^{K}Σ|e_j|`, where `K` is the level-`N` `ℓ¹` bound and is independent of `N'`.
  - Reading: the card's risk ("the dual-vector norm grows like `φ(N_Q)`") came from suppressing every character of the large level. Two cutoffs remove it: choose `N` from the coefficient tail, fix the model and `η`, then choose `N'` so that the tail beyond `N'` has mass `≤ η`. So countably many characters with absolutely summable coefficients cannot share a zero-free Bohr-lifted Euler product unless one character carries everything. This is step 5 of the limit-periodic Saias–Weingartner plan, in Lean. Module `RHTower/CharacterProductZeroPlantingTwoLevel`. Standard axioms.

- **MUST-1381 addendum (scope correction).** The "risk" that MUST-1381 was said to resolve was misstated in `1-in-progress/rational-lock-unbounded-denominators.md` (loop row 1135). That card duplicates `1-in-progress/unbounded-denominator-lock-closure.md` (row 2106), which already notes the following. By orthogonality, the suppression vector `Σ_{χ≠χ₁,χ₂} v_χ` has `ℓ¹` norm `≤ 3` at every level. So the planting constant `K ≤ |L₀| + 3R' + 1` is uniform in the level, and single-level planting with an explicit tail already works on paper. MUST-1381 is the Lean form of the infrastructure that card lists as needed ("a version of `exists_charProduct_zero` with an absolutely summable family of characters and an explicit tail"). Its two-level form additionally makes the band characters' pairings exactly `0`. No new mathematical obstruction was removed.

- **MUST-1381 addendum 2 [L] (abstract and power-series far parts).** The planting holds with any far part `Φ(S, z)` in place of `Σ_j e_jΠ_S(1−g_j(p)z_p)^{−1}`, provided that `|Φ(S, v)| ≤ η e^{2Σ_S|v_p|}` for `v` supported on `S` with `|v_p| ≤ ½`, and that `Φ` is holomorphic along holomorphic families of such `v`. The planted `z` is supported on `S` (`RHTower.CharacterZeroPlanting.exists_twoLevel_zero_of_far`; `η = |C(χ₁)|/(48e^{2K})`). The product form is re-derived as a corollary. The new instance is the power series `Φ = Σ_n τ_n f_z(n)` with `|τ_n| ≤ η`, where `f_z` is completely multiplicative with prime values `z` (`exists_twoLevel_zero_of_powerSeries`). Its size condition is the Euler bound `Σ_n|f_v(n)| = Π_S(1−|v_p|)^{−1} ≤ e^{2Σ_S|v_p|}` (`summable_norm_primeValueTwist`). Holomorphy comes from the majorant `η f_b` with `b = ½·1_S`. Reading: additive twists `Σ_n e(nx) f(n)` at frequencies `x` whose denominators exceed the level are not character products. With `f = p^{−s₀}` on small primes and `z_p` on `S`, they are power series in `z` with coefficients at most `ζ(σ₀)·Σ_{den>D}|β|`. So the C2112 M2 tail goes directly into the planting. Small perturbations `C^{(D)} − C` of the level-`N` coefficients are absorbed the same way, because `Π_S(1−ξ(p)v_p)^{−1} = Σ_n ξ(n) f_v(n)`. Module `RHTower/CharacterProductZeroPlantingTwoLevel`. Standard axioms.

- **MUST-1382 [L] (lag receivers: almost every spacing is blind, a non-meagre set is not).**
  - **Statement.** For every `Θ > 0` there is a countable configuration `ρ_i` with positive summable weights such that:
    - `½ < Re ρ_i < ½ + Θ`, and the supremum `½ + Θ` is approached but not attained;
    - the ordinates are locally finite, and the configuration is closed under conjugation;
    - the good set `G = {ℓ > 0 : sup_m Re Σ_i c_i e^{mℓ(ρ_i−½)} < ∞}` has FULL Lebesgue measure and is MEAGRE.

    (`RHTower.AlmostEverySpacing.exists_lag_configuration_goodSpacings_ae_and_meagre`; measure half alone: `exists_lag_configuration_ae_spacing_bddAbove`.)
  - **Mechanism.**
    - Fejér blocks: points `½ + δ_b + i(j−k)ω_b`, `j ≠ k < K_b`, weight `c_b/(2K_b)`. Block lag `(c_b e^{δ_b t}/2)(F_b − 1)`, with `F_b = K_b^{−1}|Σ_{k<K_b} e^{ikω_b t}|²` and `F_b sin²(ω_b t/2) ≤ 1/K_b`.
    - Parameters: `δ_b = Θ(1 − 2^{−b−1})`, `K_b = 2^{8b+8}`, `c_b = 2^{−5b(b+1)}`, `ω_b = b + 1`.
    - `Φ(t) > 0` forces `t` into a thin window `{t < τ_b, |sin(ω_b t/2)| < 2^{−3b−3}}` (`exists_block_of_pos`), so `{Φ > 0}` has finite measure (Jordan + `volume_thinWindow_le`).
    - Borel–Cantelli in the spacing (`Σ_n n^{−1}[nL ≤ s ≤ 2nL] ≤ 3`) gives the full-measure half.
    - Category half: at spike times `2πn/ω_b` in `[τ_{b−1}, σ_b]`, block `b` dominates and `F_b = K_b`, so `Φ → ∞` on every half-line (`exists_lag_gt`). `Φ` is continuous, so `{ℓ : ∀m, Φ(mℓ) ≤ M}` is closed and nowhere dense.
  - **Reading.** For zero-side receivers built on single-base lag progressions, measure and category disagree.
    - "Lags bounded along almost every base" CANNOT see a non-attained top. A metric (positive-measure, a.e.) version of the corpus Baire receiver `riemannHypothesis_iff_not_isMeagre_bddAbove_progression` (MUST-1363) is FALSE as a zero-side principle.
    - The category hypothesis MUST stay.
    - A producer for the progression receivers therefore CANNOT proceed by averaging over bases (Fubini or typical-base arguments). It MUST control a non-meagre (e.g. interval or residual) family of spacings, i.e. the classical growth form.
  - Module `RHTower/WeilLagAlmostEverySpacingBlind`. Standard axioms.

- **MUST-1383 [L] (a limit-periodic Dirichlet exponential carries a single character; C2112 step M2).** Let `ℓ(0) = ℓ(1) = 0` with `Σ|ℓ(n)|n^{−σ} < ∞` for all `σ > 1`. Suppose `exp⋆ℓ(n) = Σ_q Ψ_q(n)` (`n ≥ 1`), where `Ψ_q` has period `q+1`, `|Ψ_q| ≤ B_q` and `Σ_q √(q+1) B_q < ∞`. For a character `ξ` mod `N` put `Γ_ξ(s) = Σ_q Σ_{χ mod q+1, χ∼ξ} L(s,c_χ)L(s,χ)`. Here `χ∼ξ` means agreement at level `(q+1)N`, and `c_χ` is the `(q+1)`-smooth character section of `Ψ_q`. Then for every real `s₀ > 1` and every `N`, at most one `ξ` mod `N` has `Γ_ξ(s₀) ≠ 0` (`RHTower.CharacterZeroPlanting.limitPeriodic_exp_single_character`; `Γ` is `limitCharCoeff` and is independent of the level, `limitCharCoeff_changeLevel`).
  - Mechanism:
    - Character Parseval gives `Σ_χ|c_χ(m)| ≤ √(q+1)·sup|Ψ_q|` (`sum_norm_charSection_le`). The weight `√den` is therefore exactly the Gauss-sum size.
    - Choose the level `N₁ = N·q₀!` from the tail mass, then the cutoff `D` from `η` (Euler products `Π_{p≤D} → L(s₀,χ)`, `tendsto_nearCoeff`), then `N' = N₁·D!`.
    - Twist by `f(p) = p^{−s₀}` (`p ≤ D`), `z_p` (`p ∈ S`). Levels `< D` decompose into characters and regroup into level-`N₁` coefficients plus a band of mass `≤ Σ_{q≥q₀} W_q` (`sum_near_regroup`, `sum_norm_bandCoeff_le`). Levels `≥ D` and the coefficient error form the far part of MUST-1381 addendum 2.
    - Planting contradicts `Σ a f = exp(Σ ℓ f) ≠ 0`.
  - Scope: this is the limit-periodic extension of the Saias–Weingartner single-character rigidity (`periodic_exp_single_character`), with infinitely many periods and an `ℓ¹(√den)` bound. It is M2 of `1-in-progress/unbounded-denominator-lock-closure.md`. The remaining C2112 steps are M1 (the lock produces such an expansion: Hurwitz continuation and boundary uniqueness) and M3 (pole at `1` forces `ξ` principal, then RH), both paper-only. Module `RHTower/LimitPeriodicExpSingleCharacter`. Standard axioms.

- **MUST-1384 [L] (one-sided lag bounds force every positive locally finite configuration on-line; positive survivor of MUST-1382).**
  - **Statement.** Let `ι` be countable, `c_i > 0` with `Σ c_i < ∞`, and `w_i ∈ ℂ` with `Re w_i ≤ B` and only finitely many `w_i` in each disc. Put `Φ(t) = Re Σ_i c_i e^{t w_i}`.
    - If `Φ(t) ≤ M` for all `t ≥ s₀`, then `Re w_i ≤ 0` for every `i` (`RHTower.OneSidedConfiguration.re_nonpos_of_lag_le`).
    - If the set `{ℓ > 0 : m ↦ Φ(mℓ) is bounded above}` is not meagre, then `Re w_i ≤ 0` for every `i` (`re_nonpos_of_not_isMeagre`).
    - For complex weights: if every real exponent `w_i > 0` carries `Re a_i > 0` and `Re Σ a_i e^{t w_i} ≤ M` on `[0, ∞)`, then no exponent is real and positive (`re_nonpos_of_real`).
  - **Mechanism.**
    - *Landau across a real pole* (`false_of_realPole`). Suppose `φ ≤ M` on `[0, ∞)`, its transform `Λ` is analytic at the real points `t > p > 0`, and `Re Λ` is unbounded above on `(p, ∞)`. Then the transform of `(M − φ)₊du + du` has abscissa `c` and equals `(M+1)/s − Λ` on `(max(c, p), ∞)`. Either positivity fails near `p`, or Landau's singularity at `c` fails.
    - *Blow-up* (`exists_re_pairSeries_ge`). At the largest real exponent `p = w_j`, `Re Λ(σ) ≥ Re a_j/(σ − p) − 2Σ‖a‖/η`, where `η` is the local-finiteness gap at `p`.
    - *Twist*. `Φ(t)(1 + cos(t Im w_j))` is the lag function of `{w_i, w_i ± i Im w_j}` with weights `c_i(1, ½, ½) > 0`. It is still one-sided bounded, and it has the real exponent `Re w_j`. This reduces the theorem to real exponents with no identity theorem off the real axis.
    - *Baire*. The level sets `{ℓ ≥ 1/(k+1) : ∀m, Φ(mℓ) ≤ M}` are closed. A non-meagre union contains an interval of spacings, so `Φ ≤ M` on a half-line (`exists_nat_mul_mem_Ioo`).
  - **Reading.**
    - MUST-1363's Baire receiver needs nothing about `ζ` beyond positivity of the weights and local finiteness. Together with MUST-1382 this gives an exact dichotomy for one-sided progression receivers on positive configurations: category is rigid for every configuration, while measure is blind for some.
    - A producer for this receiver class MUST deliver a one-sided bound on a non-meagre set of spacings, which is equivalent to a half-line bound, i.e. the classical one-sided form of `RH ⟺ Φ bdd above` (`riemannHypothesis_iff_weilLagFunctionReal_bddAbove`). Nothing weaker in this class can be sufficient, and nothing beyond positivity and local finiteness of the zero side is used.
    - Signed weights are not covered. The twist needs `1 + cos ≥ 0` against positive weights.
  - Module `RHTower/WeilLagOneSidedConfigurationRigidity`. Standard axioms.

- **MUST-1385 [L] (a producer with limit-periodic coefficients forces RH; C2112 step M3).** Let `G` be holomorphic on `Re s > ½` with `G' = ΦG`, where `Φ` is holomorphic there. Let `G` be continuous on `Re s ≥ ½` and equal to `s(s−1)Γ_ℝ(s)F(s)` on `Re s > 1`, with `F = exp(Σ lam(n)n^{−s}/log n) = Σ a(n)n^{−s}`. Suppose `a(n) = Σ_q Ψ_q(n)`, where `Ψ_q` has period `q+1`, `|Ψ_q| ≤ B_q` and `Σ_q √(q+1)·8^{ω(q+1)}·B_q < ∞`. Then RH holds (`RHTower.AbelianTwist.limitPeriodic_producer_riemannHypothesis`). No Herglotz positivity `Re Φ ≥ 0` is used.
  - Mechanism:
    - `F = Σ_q Σ_χ L(s,c_χ)L(s,χ)` (`LSeries_limitPeriodic`, `LSeries_periodic_eq_sum`).
    - At `s → 1⁺` only the trivial characters keep a pole. So `(s−1)F(s) → A(1)` with `A(s) = Σ_q L(s,c_{q,1})Π_{p|q+1}(1−p^{−s})`. The proof uses dominated convergence with `(s−1)|L(s,χ)| ≤ 2` and Parseval over the smooth numbers (`tendsto_sub_one_mul_limitPeriodic`). Since `G(1) ≠ 0`, `A(1) ≠ 0`.
    - `A` is holomorphic on `Re s > ½`, with bound `8^{ω(q+1)}B_q`.
    - Near `1⁺`, `Γ_1 = ζA ≠ 0` (`limitCharCoeff_one_eq`). So MUST-1383 kills every other class at every level `k!`, and the class decomposition (`norm_sub_sum_limitCharCoeff_le`) gives `F = ζA`. By the identity theorem, `G = s(s−1)Γ_ℝζA` on `Re s > ½`, and `G_ne_zero` gives RH.
  - Scope: this is the limit-periodic extension of the bounded-denominator endgame (MUST-1327 steps 2–5). It reduces C2112 (unbounded-denominator rational locks ⟹ RH) to M1: a lock `G(1−s) = (Σ_j q_j u_j^{−(s−½)})G(s)` with rational `u_j` must produce such an expansion with `Σ_x|β(x)|den(x)^{½+ε} < ∞` (`8^{ω(n)} ≪_ε n^ε`). The period law at every real height is already in Lean (`tendsto_far_real_height`, `tendsto_far_translation`). What remains for M1 is the Hurwitz continuation of `F·V = Σ_{x₀}P(x₀)ζ(s,x₀)` with uniform bounds, plus the boundary-uniqueness and Bohr steps. Module `RHTower/LimitPeriodicProducerRH`. Standard axioms.

- **MUST-1384 addendum [L] (complex weights; the abstract receiver at L-function generality).**
  - **Statement.** Let the exponents `w_i` be distinct and locally finite, with `0 ≤ Im w_i` (one exponent per conjugate pair) and `Re w_i ≤ B`. Let the weights be nonzero with `Σ‖a_i‖ < ∞`, and put `Φ(t) = Re Σ a_i e^{t w_i}`.
    - If `Φ ≤ M` on a half-line and `Re a_i > 0` at every real exponent, then all `Re w_i ≤ 0` (`RHTower.OneSidedConfiguration.re_nonpos_of_lagRe_le_upper`).
    - If `|Φ| ≤ M` on a half-line and `Re a_i ≠ 0` at every real exponent, then all `Re w_i ≤ 0` (`re_nonpos_of_abs_lagRe_le_upper`).
    - The same conclusions follow from bounds along a non-meagre set of progressions (`re_nonpos_of_not_isMeagre_upper`, `re_nonpos_of_not_isMeagre_abs_upper`). The generic Baire step is `exists_halfLine_le_of_not_isMeagre`.

    - The core needs positivity only at the TOPMOST real exponent (`MaxRealPositive`).
    - The phase twist `1 + cos(t Im w_k + arg a_k)`, at the rightmost exponent `w_k` of the height of an off-line `w_j`, makes `Re w_k` the largest real exponent, with the single weight `|a_k|e^{s₁Re w_k}/2 > 0`.
    - In the two-sided case, `±Φ` handles real exponents of either sign.
  - **Reading.**
    - This shape covers `ζ` (weights `2m_ρ/(ρ(1−ρ))`, no real zeros) and every L-function whose real zeros have positive weight `1/(β(1−β))`.
    - So the Baire/half-line rigidity of one-sided lag receivers is a theorem about locally finite configurations, not about arithmetic.
    - With MUST-1379(i) (no local finiteness: blind on all of `|s| ≥ ε`) and MUST-1382 (measure: blind), local finiteness plus category is the exact rigidity condition for zero-side progression receivers.
    - Producer consequence unchanged: the producer MUST deliver the classical half-line bound.

- **MUST-1392 addendum [L] (subexponential precision gives AAL).** Suppose that for every `a > 0` there are `M` and a measurable finite-measure set `E` with `Φ(L) ≤ M e^{aL}` for all `L ≥ 0`, `L ∉ E`. In ψ terms the condition reads `ψ(x) ≥ x − C_ε x^{½+ε}` for every `ε > 0`, outside a set of finite logarithmic measure. This is far below the √x precision that RH-strength producers need: AAL costs only subexponential one-sided precision off finite measure, so all RH content beyond it is the large-height half (ZAL). Combine it with the Laplace bound `Re Σ a_i/(σ−w_i) ≤ max(M,0)/σ + W∫_E e^{−(σ−B)u}`. Upper density zero ⇒ Abel density zero follows by Tonelli (`abelDensityZero_of_upperDensityZero`).

    - `Φ ≤ M e^{aL}` off an Abel-density-zero set, together with an attained top `β₀`, gives `β₀ ≤ ½ + a`.

    - This strictly strengthens MUST-1392: finite measure is replaced by density zero, so exceptional scale sets of infinite measure such as `∪_k [k², k²+1]` are tolerated.

  - Module `RHTower/WeilLagFunctionDensityZeroExcursion`. Standard axioms.

    - Fix `ε` with `|V(½+ε−iy) − v(y)| ≤ ½`. Apply the argument principle for `E` on `[½−ε, σ₀]×[Y₀,Y]` and for `A` on `[½+ε, σ₀]×[−Y,−Y₀]`. This bounds the phase advance of `V(½+ε−i·)` above by `4π + 2C_E + 2C_A`: the enclosed zeros only lower it, the horizontal edges are bounded by Backlund–Jensen, and the edges at `σ₀` by `2π`.

    - The frontier item "two-sided rational spectra with positive mean motion" is now closed in the strongest form. No weighted AP lock has positive mean motion, and the only Herglotz producer carrying one is the true producer.

      - a Backlund–Jensen horizontal bound for any bounded holomorphic function with a positive real part at the disc centre (`abs_integral_im_logDeriv_horizontal_le`).
  - Modules `RHTower/LocalRectangleArgumentBound`, `RHTower/WeilAlmostPeriodicLockTrueProducer` (refactors: `limitPeriodic_producer_factor`, `almostPeriodicLock_limitPeriodic`). Standard axioms.

    - RH ⟺ ¬chain ∧ ∃M: `{Φ > M}` has upper density zero;
    - RH ⟺ ¬chain ∧ JAS level-one interval positivity off a set of log-scales of upper density zero.
    - Compare the corpus capstone RH ⟺ JasDressedPSD 1 ∧ ¬chain: with the same side condition, the positivity may now fail on any density-zero set of scales.
  - Module `RHTower/WeilLagFunctionDensityZeroExcursion`. Standard axioms.

- **MUST-1393 addendum 2 [L] (lower density zero suffices).**
  - **Abstract.** The core inequality `Re Σ_{w_i=B} a_i ≤ δ Σ|a_i|` needs `η∫_E e^{−ηu} ≤ δ` only along some sequence `η → 0⁺`, i.e. lower Abel density.
  - **Conversion.** Lower density zero (`|E ∩ [0,T_n]| = o(T_n)` along some `T_n → ∞`) ⇒ lower Abel density zero, by the split `J_E(η) ≤ |E∩[0,T]| + e^{−ηT}/η` with `ηT = 2/d`.
  - **For ζ.**
    - RH ⟺ ¬JasOffLineChain ∧ ∃M: `{Φ > M}` has lower density zero.
    - RH ⟺ ¬JasOffLineChain ∧ JAS level-one interval positivity off a set of log-scales of lower density zero.
  - **Reading.**
    - The exceptional scale set may have upper density one. For example, with `T_{n+1} = T_n³` the JAS tests may fail at every scale with `log y ∈ [T_n, T_n²]`. With the side condition ¬chain, a producer needs to succeed only on most scales below `T_n` for a sequence `T_n → ∞`.
    - Sharpness: an attained top forces positive lower density, so no positive density threshold is tolerated uniformly.
  - Module `RHTower/WeilLagFunctionDensityZeroExcursion`. Standard axioms.

- **MUST-1394 addendum [L] (the log moment is not needed).**
  - `almostPeriodicLock_trueProducer` now holds under exactly the MUST-1391 hypothesis `Σ_j|c_j|max(1,u_j^{−1})K(u_j) < ∞`. The condition `Σ|c_j||log u_j| < ∞` is dropped. So every Herglotz producer with a weighted almost-periodic lock is the true producer.
  - **Mechanism.**
    - The lock phase is taken as a continuous lift `θ` of `v = V(½−i·)`, not as an integral of a velocity (the velocity needs the log moment).
    - Monotonicity of `θ` comes from the local positivity law at non-zeros of `G`. The zeros of `G` on the line are locally finite, because `A` glues holomorphically across the line (`lineFactor_lowerZeros_finite`). A finite-exception local-to-global lemma does the rest (`le_of_locally_monotone_off_finite`).
    - The upper bound comes from the rectangle bound (`apLock_shiftedPhase_bound`) and a lift comparison (`phase_sub_le_of_shift`).
    - The monotone twist theorem (`abelian_twist_power_rigidity`) finishes.
  - Module `RHTower/WeilAlmostPeriodicLockTrueProducer` (split into four declarations). Standard axioms.

- **MUST-1395 [L] (route JAS needs only one geometric progression of scales, given attainment).**
  - **Growth-majorant single-base lemma** (`exists_lag_progression_gt_exp_of_attainedTop`). If the top `β₀` is attained and `a < β₀ − ½`, then for every spacing `ℓ > 0` and every `M` some `Φ(mℓ) > M e^{a mℓ}`. This is the corpus Dirichlet argument with the majorant built into the final numerics.
  - **Capstones.** For every `ℓ > 0`:
    - RH ⟺ ¬JasOffLineChain ∧ ∃X: level-one constant-vector interval positivity on every `(y, y+L]` with `y = e^{mℓ}` (`riemannHypothesis_iff_not_jasOffLineChain_and_jasProgressionPositive`);
    - the same with ZAL in place of ¬chain;
    - the dyadic form `y = 2^m` (`riemannHypothesis_iff_not_jasOffLineChain_and_jasDyadicScalesPositive`).
  - **Mechanism.** The diagonal Bochner window bound is pointwise in the scale. With the exceptional set equal to the complement of the progression it gives `|Φ(mℓ)| ≤ M e^{(15α/16)mℓ}`, which contradicts the lemma.
  - **Reading: complete exception law for constant-vector JAS.**
    - Without a side condition: all scales, or all scales off an exponentially thin set (MUST-1390). Subexponential exceptions down to the Paley–Wiener threshold are conjectural.
    - With ¬chain: either one geometric progression of scales (a set of measure zero), or all scales off a set of lower density zero (MUST-1393).
    - Sparse-scale positivity cannot see chains: single-base Wolff and Fejér configurations are blind. So the attainment half of RH is extremely cheap for JAS producers, and all difficulty sits in chain exclusion.
  - Modules `RHTower/JointAncestryProgressionScales` and `RHTower/JointAncestryChainAttainmentSplit`. The latter gives RH ⟺ quasi-RH ∧ window positivity ∧ constant-vector positivity off lower-density-zero scales. Standard axioms.

- **MUST-1396 [L] (a bounded ζ-quotient and a continuous lock force the true producer; almost periodicity is only needed for the factorization).**
  - **Statement.** Let `G` be a Herglotz producer for `lam` with `G = s(s−1)Γ_ℝ(s)ζ(s)A(s)` on `Re s > ½` (`s ≠ 1`), where `A` is holomorphic on `Re s > ½` and continuous and bounded on `Re s ≥ ½`. Let the lower-line lock `G(1−s) = V(s)G(s)` hold with `V` continuous, bounded, holomorphic on `½ < Re s < 3/2`, and `|V(½+ε−iy) − V(½−iy)| ≤ ½` for one `ε ∈ (0,¼]` and all `y`. The last condition holds whenever `V` is uniformly continuous on the closed strip (`exists_shift_close_of_uniformContinuousOn`). Then `lam(n) = Λ(n)` for `n ≥ 2`, and RH holds (`RHTower.AbelianTwist.boundedQuotient_lock_trueProducer`).
  - MUST-1394 is now its corollary (`almostPeriodicLock_trueProducer`): the almost-periodic chain supplies `A`, and `apLock` satisfies the lock conditions.
  - **Reading.** For the uniqueness half of HF, the only obstruction is an unbounded quotient `G/(s(s−1)Γ_ℝζ)` near the critical line or a discontinuous lock. Both occur exactly in the twin door (fractional atoms, `A ~ ζ^{m−1}`, step phases). Any producer route that yields a bounded quotient and a uniformly continuous lock lands on `Λ`.
  - Module `RHTower/WeilAlmostPeriodicLockTrueProducer`. Standard axioms.

- **MUST-1397 [L] (under quasi-RH, route JAS lives on a doubly exponentially sparse test family).**
  - **Uniform window conditions** (`eventually_window_conditions_uniform`). The twelve window conditions of the quasi-RH chain exclusion hold eventually uniformly in `θ ∈ [θ₂/2, θ₂]` with `ε = θc₀/300`.
    - Most conditions are monotone in `(θ, ε)` and are taken at the extreme parameters.
    - The scale conditions use the θ-uniform threshold bound and `x^{s(θ)} ≥ x^{s(θ₁)}`.
    - The cut condition holds pointwise for `x ≥ 3`.
  - **Chain exclusion on chain-rich windows** (`one_add_sSup_le_of_jasWindowPositivityOn_of_chain`). Window positivity is needed only on a set `W` with the property: for every large peak height γ, some `θ ∈ [θ₂/2, θ₂]` has `⌊γ^{75/θ}⌋ ∈ W`. The proof chooses θ after the peak.
  - **Doubly exponential windows are chain-rich** (`chainRichWindows_doubleExp`): `θ = 75 log γ/(2^k log 2)` makes the index exactly `2^{2^k}`.
  - **Capstone** (`riemannHypothesis_iff_quasi_and_doubleExpWindows_and_dyadicScales`). RH ⟺ quasi-RH ∧ level-one log-weight window positivity on `(2^{2^k}, 2^{2^{k+1}}]` ∧ level-one constant-vector positivity at the dyadic scales `y = 2^m`.
  - **Reading.** Under quasi-RH, all RH content of route JAS sits in two sparse families:
    - doubly exponential windows, which exclude chains;
    - one geometric progression of scales, which excludes attained tops.

    The corpus capstone RH ⟺ JasDressedPSD 1 ∧ quasi-RH thus reduces to two countable, very sparse test families.
  - Module `RHTower/JointAncestrySparseChainExclusion`. Standard axioms.

- **MUST-1396 addendum [L] (size is no obstruction: sub-linear-exponential quotient growth suffices).**
  - `RHTower.AbelianTwist.slowQuotient_lock_trueProducer`: the conclusion of MUST-1396 (`lam = Λ` and RH) holds when the quotient only satisfies `|A(s)| ≤ W e^{|Im s|^α}` on `Re s ≥ ½`, for some `α < 1`; `A` need not be bounded. The bounded case is the corollary `α = 0`.
  - Mechanism. The Backlund–Jensen constants grow like `Y^α`, so the lock phase is `O(y^α)`. The monotone twist theorem holds below the linear wall.
  - Reading. A Herglotz producer with a continuous lock is forced to `Λ` unless its quotient `G/(s(s−1)Γ_ℝζ)` is singular at the critical line: discontinuous, i.e. `G` fails to vanish at a ζ-zero to full order; or growing at least like `e^{|t|}`. The twin door (`A ~ ζ^{m−1}`) is of the first kind. So the uniqueness obstruction is divisor-supported, not size.
  - Generic lemmas: `glue_horizontal_le`, `quotient_horizontal_le`, `backlund_const_exp`, `norm_lockGlue_le_exp`. Standard axioms.
  - Correction to the reading above: the size exception is "not `O(e^{|t|^α})` for any `α < 1`", not "at least `e^{|t|}`". Growth such as `e^{|t|/log|t|}` is not covered.

- **MUST-1397 addendum [L] (purely JAS sparse capstone).** RH ⟺ the single-prime tests on large primes are positive at some level `σ < ½` ∧ level-one log-weight window positivity on `(2^{2^k}, 2^{2^{k+1}}]` ∧ level-one constant-vector positivity at the dyadic scales (`riemannHypothesis_iff_singlePrime_and_doubleExpWindows_and_dyadicScales`). The single-prime tests supply the half-plane `Re ρ ≤ ½ + max(σ, ¼)`, and the sparse families do the rest. This sharpens the corpus JAS-internal capstone (single-prime ∧ product positivity on all large-prime sets). Module `RHTower/JointAncestrySparseChainExclusion`.
